time.desc: One party announced the immediate suspension of bilateral trade negotiations on the grounds of the other party's digital service tax, and stated that it would unilaterally set new tariff rates and cutoffs by notification soon.

One party announces that it has reached a tariff framework deal with a trading partner, which includes provisions for setting higher tax rates for transshipment avoidance, and uses this as a phased outcome of tariff negotiations.

An organization released a quantitative analysis, estimating that the tariff plan will cost tens of billions of dollars in direct costs for medium-sized enterprises in the sponsoring countries, equivalent to about US$2,000 per employee, which contradicts the sponsor's statement that foreign manufacturers will bear the tariffs.
One party announced that it would replace the one-by-one negotiation model with "mass sending tariff letters" and directly inform many countries of the tariff rates that will apply to their exports.

The 'transshipment' clause in the tariff framework for a manufacturing hub partner triggered violent market fluctuations. The stock prices of related apparel and manufacturing companies initially rose due to optimism and then fell sharply for several hours.

One party issued formal tariff letters to many countries and extended the negotiation period to a new node, making it clear that if an arrangement is not reached, higher range tariffs will be triggered with the threat of countermeasures and anti-transshipment.
News that the sponsoring country had imposed additional tariffs on imports of an industrial metal caused the price of the metal to surge, recording the largest one-day rise in decades.

The leader of the initiating country announced an increase in tariffs on imported goods from a long-term ally, and changed the country's evaluation from "tough" to "spoiled". The ally has sent representatives to the negotiation venue many times since the beginning of the year.

A subsidiary of a regional group responded urgently, stating that it would speed up negotiations with the sponsoring country and strive to reach a mutually beneficial agreement before the new tariffs take effect.

The head of government of an allied country publicly stated that the sponsoring country's tax increase decision was "extremely regrettable", but pointed out that the announced tax rate was lower than the previously threatened level, leaving room for further negotiations.

One party announced the imposition of substantial tariffs on the import of key industrial metals and announced high tariffs on more industries. At the same time, it publicly equated the "tariff letter with an agreement" mechanism.
Leaders of sponsoring countries predict 'very high' tariffs on drugs will soon be imposed

The leader of the initiating country announced a new tariff on imported goods from a neighboring country and planned to increase the general tariff from 10% to a maximum of 20%, claiming that 'all remaining countries will pay the price'

The leadership of a manufacturing hub partner was surprised by the tariff framework rate announced by the sponsoring country and instructed the negotiation team to continue working hard to lower the rate.

The leader of the initiating country wrote a letter announcing the imposition of high tariffs on a neighboring country's products. The reasons include drug inflow, trade deficit and the country's dairy supply management system.

The Prime Minister's Office of a neighboring country responded that it would convene a cabinet meeting and a meeting of provincial governors to focus on negotiations, and stated that it would firmly defend its workers and companies until the revised cutoff.

One party announced the imposition of higher uniform tariff levels on the products of regional economic groups and its member countries, overturned the previous principled negotiation framework of lower tax rates and warned that it would retaliate by superimposing tax increases.

In response to the tariff letter from the sponsoring country, the head of a neighboring country expressed confidence that an agreement can be reached before the tariffs take effect, but emphasized that his country's sovereignty must not be negotiated.

The head of a regional group committee responded that high tariffs will disrupt cross-border supply chains and harm the interests of businesses and consumers on both sides of the Taiwan Strait, but still hopes to persuade the sponsoring country to make concessions.

Leaders of the sponsoring countries issued tariff threats to about twenty-five trading partners within a week, requiring them to sign a trade agreement that meets the requirements before the cutoff, otherwise they will face punitive tariffs
A regional group officially released a retaliation list, including chemicals and plastics among the products to be subject to additional tariffs.
The head of a major country in the southern hemisphere has publicly threatened to impose a 50% retaliatory tariff on its goods if the sponsoring country raises taxes as scheduled.

Faced with preparations for retaliation, the leaders of the sponsoring countries softened their tone significantly in an interview, saying "I don't know how they can retaliate" and stating that the group "is treating us very well now."

The initiating country reached a trade agreement with a long-term ally, lowering the country's import tariffs from previously threatened levels. The other party promised to invest heavily in the initiating country and open its market, while also lowering auto tariffs.

The two major economies confirmed their agreement to extend the tariff truce. The financial chief of the sponsoring country said that the other party's representative was "a little too hasty" and said that the leaders will make a final decision on whether to maintain the truce within two weeks.

One party signed an executive order to cancel the tariff exemption for low-value packages and significantly advance the implementation time and expand it to the world. At the same time, it clarified the scope of application and effective date of high tariffs on some copper products.

On the same day, the sponsoring country announced that it would impose a 50% tariff on some semi-processed metal products and it will take effect soon. After the news was announced, the metal futures plummeted by nearly 20%, erasing the recent premium accumulated over the global benchmark price.

The judiciary held a key hearing and publicly questioned the president's legal authority to impose large-scale unilateral tariffs. At the same time, a new round of "reciprocal" tariffs officially came into effect on the same day.
The initiating country's new round of 'reciprocal' tariffs officially takes effect within a set period, covering dozens of countries, with tax rates ranging from 10% to 40%
A major country in the southern hemisphere was slapped with an additional 40% tariff by the sponsoring country due to the trial of its former president, raising the total tax rate to 50%.

The sponsoring country threatened to impose an additional 2.5% tariff on an energy importing country, raising the total tax rate to 50%, on the grounds that the country purchased oil from the conflict party and gave it several weeks to respond.

At the set cutoff, one side raised import tariffs on its neighbors on the grounds of insufficient border security and anti-drug cooperation, while the other side emphasized that exemptions from existing agreements and negotiations are still continuing.

The ambassador and chief negotiator of a neighboring country to the sponsoring country responded that it had a professional and constructive dialogue with the other party this week, and pointed out that the exemption of goods that comply with existing agreements puts the country in a better position than most countries

The ruling party announced the implementation of a package of punitive tariffs on many countries, covering steel, aluminum, automobiles, agricultural products, etc., ranging from poor small countries to wealthy partners.
A central bank kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged due to economic uncertainty caused by tariffs. Business investment became cautious and consumer confidence declined.

The foreign affairs department of an energy-importing country responded publicly for the first time and criticized the sponsoring country's tariff threat as "unfair and unreasonable" and countered that the other country itself was still trading with the conflicting party.

One party officially launched a policy of imposing extremely high tariffs on semiconductors and set up an exemption and recovery mechanism for local factory construction commitments. At the same time, it imposed additional tariffs on major emerging economies as geopolitical punishment.

The sponsoring country officially imposed an additional 2.5% tariff on imported goods from an energy importing country, raising the total tax rate to 50%. The government responded by calling the move "unfair, unreasonable, and without justification."

The authorities of a technology-producing area submitted formal opinions to the sponsoring country on semiconductor tariffs and sought exemptions, warning that tax increases would increase companies' production costs and reduce their willingness to invest in the country.

The 20% tariff imposed by the sponsoring country on goods from a certain technological origin has officially come into effect, affecting the export of machine tools, plastic products, orchids, seafood and other agricultural products.
Many regional central banks unexpectedly cut interest rates to defend against the impact of the trade war, and a trend of regional monetary easing is taking shape.

For the first time, a head of state from a neighboring country publicly announced that he is studying the imposition of additional tariffs on imported goods that have not signed a free trade agreement with his country, aiming to cope with the pressure of the trade war and prevent his country from becoming a transit point for cheap goods.

The highest judicial body agreed to expedite the trial of the dispute over the president's extensive tariff authority and scheduled the hearing to this year, and to keep the tariffs in effect until the ruling.

During a meeting with officials from a regional group, the leader of the sponsoring country called on the group to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the two main buyers of oil from the conflict parties to put pressure on ending a certain conflict.

The two major economies held a new round (the fourth round) of negotiations to extend the temporary tariff truce. The topics covered national security, economy and trade, the divestiture of a short video application, and cooperation in combating money laundering networks.

The sponsoring country's trade authorities have officially launched a review process for a regional comprehensive trade agreement, launching dozens of days of public consultation and planning to hold public hearings later.
